source_refs.note: 2) External pressure: a main subheading of 5.9.1 Factors affecting the boiling points of liquids, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 107-108.

blocks.text: As already explained that when vapour pressure of a liquid becomes equal to the external pressure then the liquid boils. It means that when external pressure is changed, its boiling point will also change. When the external pressure is high the liquid requires greater amount of heat to equalize its vapour pressure to external pressure. In this way boiling point is raised. Similarly, at a lower external pressure a liquid absorbs less amount of heat and it boils at a lower temperature.

For example, water shows B.P of 120 °C at 1489 torr pressure and boils at 25 °C at 23.7 torr. Water boils at 98 °C at Murree hills due to external pressure of 700 torr while at the top of Mount Everest water boils at only 69 °C at 323 torr.
book_errors: water boils at only 69 °C at 323 torr

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: These two numbers do not match: at 323 torr water boils at about 78 °C, and at 69 °C its vapour pressure is only about 223 torr. At the top of Mount Everest the air pressure is about 250 torr, so water boils there at about 70 °C.

We can increase the external pressure artificially on the surface of boiling water by using a pressure cooker. Pressure cooker is a closed container. The vapour of water formed is not allowed to escape. In this way, it exerts they develop more pressure on the water surface in the cooker and the boiling temperature increases. As more heat is absorbed in water, so food is cooked quickly under increased pressure.

blocks.prompt: a) Why food cooking is difficult in the areas with high altitudes?
blocks.explanation: At high altitude the air pressure is lower, so water boils below 100 °C (98 °C at Murree). Food cooks more slowly in this less hot water.

blocks.prompt: b) The food cooks faster in the pressure cooker, explain.
blocks.explanation: A pressure cooker does not let the vapour escape, so the pressure inside rises and water boils above 100 °C. The hotter water cooks the food faster.

blocks.prompt: c) Why the boiling point of water (100 ℃) is higher than that of ethanol (78 ℃), although both have hydrogen bonds?
blocks.explanation: On average each water molecule forms two hydrogen bonds (through its two H atoms and two lone pairs), while ethanol has only one O−H. The forces in water are stronger and its vapour pressure is lower, so its boiling point is higher.
